title: The Catalan triangle Laurent polynomial and positivity conjecture
source: Victor J. W. Guo and Xiuguo Lian, “Proofs of two conjectures on Catalan triangle numbers”, arXiv:1806.02685 (2018). (https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.02685), Conjecture 6.1

lanes.final_paper_definition_and_prior_art_che: final-paper-check-381408-opus-20261119-r1/CHECK-381408.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised paper used)

significance.root_decision: For positive integers n_1, ..., n_m with n_{m+1} = n_1, an integer j, and nonnegative integers a, r with a <= n_1, the Guo-Lian q-Catalan-triangle expression (a quotient of a sum of products of Gaussian binomial coefficients, weighted by [2k][k]^(2r) q^(j k^2 - (r+1) k)) is a Laurent polynomial in q with integer coefficients for every integer j, and all its coefficients are nonnegative for 0 <= j <= m. This is Conjecture 6.1 of Guo and Lian, who proved integrality for 0 <= j <= m. The proof introduces a nonnegative Newton-type basis in which the signed recurrence acts positively, and uses interpolation at the roots of the denominator. The range 0 <= j <= m for nonnegativity is sharp (written proof only). MathDB 339461 is a duplicate record of the same conjecture and is credited once.
significance.caveat: MathDB 339461 is a duplicate record; submit once and reference both. The full text of Li and Wang (2026) on q-Narayana divisibility is unread (publisher blocks automated access); its abstract concerns a different conjecture. The sharpness of the range is proved on paper only.

root_basis: Root extracted the twelve modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the author build, axioms exactly the allowed three), and screened the omega registry. An independent Opus referee checked that the Lean statement is literal and cannot hold vacuously, read the paper line by line, ran about 65,000 exact test cases, and did a further prior-art pass; its editorially revised copy is the accepted paper.
